title: relay learns from each mistake
what: Principle 6 rewritten as above; the checker writes mistake_kind and prevent on each counted finding and the record check refuses a counted finding without them; agent runs that end without their report are recorded automatically; `relay queue mistakes` counts recurrences, a repeat counting only when the defect was written after the previous fix landed (git blame); text lessons marked and retired by ablation in the paid run; kinds assigned once to the 59 closed fix items. The kind-level guards found by the design (a hook refusing a gate wait from an agent; a temporary HOME plus main-checkout-unchanged test; programs run by subprocess listed in deps.toml) become fix items of their own.
why: Owner, 27 Oct: "Когда мы допускаем ошибку необходимо не только не только придумать способ их автоматического отлова но и способ снижения их появления в будущем / Наш gate строгий, если ошибка есть он точно её отловит / Но должен быть способ не допускать подобных ошибок в будущем - учиться на своих ошибках / Последнее звучит как принцип - учиться на своих ошибках, вероятно будущие модели будут лишены недостатков предыдущих, и рекомендации будут лишь тратить место однако сам принцип обучения на ошибках важен". Memory management deferred by the owner the same day. Owner's answers to the design's questions, 27 Oct: "1. A" (mistake kind and prevention recorded on fix items and on MEDIUM+ review findings: 236 in 22-27 Oct, about 40 checker lines a day), "2. A" (a text lesson is retired only after 20+ green runs without it, every 30 days and on a model change, about $1.70 a lesson), "3. A" (a thinker assigns kinds to the 59 closed fix items with a check record, about 30 agent minutes). Measured 22-27 Oct: 122 fix items, 396 unique findings (HIGH 100, MEDIUM 157, LOW 139); "agent ends without its report" recurred 9 times after 2 code fixes and was never filed (13 workflow StructuredOutput failures and 3 turn-limit stops seen only in the transcript); lessons kept only as text recurred in 3 of 3 kinds; the reply-style rule grew from 1,801 to 5,620 bytes in 12 commits; 24.4 kB of rule text is read every session. Proposed principle (design, front's wording, owner saw it): principle 6 becomes "Learn from each mistake: cause, not symptom": every MEDIUM+ mistake ends in a catch for its kind and a change to what produced it, or a stated reason why not; prefer making it impossible, then a guard or test over the whole kind, then a step in the template or script, then a brief line, prose last and tied to the eval that shows it is still needed. Design (redo against the fresh repository when taken): scratchpad report design-learn-from-mistakes.md of 27 Oct, without its memory-inbox change. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).

fact: Migration 27 Oct: the link in `why` line 1 points to a session file (`reports/design-learn-from-mistakes.md`, 27 Oct (without its memory-inbox change)), which is deleted when the machine restarts; the facts it held that this item rests on are the notes below.

Measured 22-27 Oct (learn-from-mistakes design): lessons kept only as text repeated in all three kinds that had one; a lesson in code held better only when it closed a whole kind of mistake, not one case. An agent that ends without handing in its report repeated 9 times after the second fix and none was queued; a test or tool writing outside its own folder was found 9 more times, 5 of the 9 defects in the code before the first fix (a test per case missed the rest); relay using a tool or Python version missing from its list repeated (`md5sum`, `ps`, fractional numbers in Python 3.11); a rule of 24 Oct did not stop a wrong number on 27 Oct; the style rule grew from 1.8 to 5.6 KB in 12 commits and two paid runs went red.
